articleTitle: Professional Teaching Practice Through MIAP based Integrated Learning Activities for Electrical Engineering Education
abstract: The purposes of the research were 1) to manage the integrated learning activities based on the MIAP learning model for professional teaching practice supporting electrical engineering education, 2) to construct and evaluate the developed instructional package on basic electric circuit, and 3) to evaluate students' satisfaction. The research tools consisted of the teacher's manual, MIAP based learning activity plan, teaching aids, and rating-scale questionnaires for contentment. The purposive sampling of this research were 12 bachelor students who enrolled in the first semester of the academic year 2020, Department of Teacher Training for Electrical Engineering, Faculty of Technical Education at King Mongkut's University of Technology North Bangkok. The research result shown that the quality of the developed MIAP based learning activities and instructional package was at a high level and the mean of satisfaction of the sampling group was also at a high level. In conclusion, from the above results, one can see that the MIAP based integrated learning activities can promote in practicing of professional teaching for electrical engineering education. The obtained result can be applied efficiently in the learning and teaching of education 4.0 era.

articleTitle: Anticipated and Actual Challenges Pertaining to Online Delivery of University Courses During COVID-19 Pandemic: The Engineering Faculty’s Experience at Assumption University
abstract: This paper describes the various challenges associated with online delivery of engineering courses at Assumption University of Thailand (AU) during the global Coronavirus 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. As COVID-19 became a widespread global crisis, educational institutions around the world were heavily impacted due to the government imposed lockdown and social distancing measures. Responses from various educational institutions varied from completely ceasing learning activities to adopting a fully online delivery mode. In the face of this sudden, disruptive shift, AU responded by switching its program delivery across all faculties to a fully online mode from the middle of March, 2020 until further notice. This significant undertaking involved anticipating challenges associated with online program delivery and acting accordingly to ensure the best possible outcome for all parties involved. Based on AU's engineering faculty's experience, the key challenges in effectively delivering online education appeared to be around technology infrastructure, learning curve, accessibility, effectiveness and suitability with specific course types, assessment of students' performance, and exam integrity. We discuss the anticipated and actual challenges, as well as the measures that were taken by engineering faculty members and decision makers to make this online learning experience effective for all participants.

articleTitle: The Effect of Blended Learning with Collaborative Learning upon English Communication Skills of English Teaching Program Students
abstract: English communication is one of the most important skills in 21st century because English is an international language. People use it for communication all over the world. It is necessary for students to improve their English skills, especially students in English teaching programs. They are able to develop their communication skills for their further studies and their future careers. Furthermore, English is used through myriads media and technologies including social media, applications, and websites. Computing and ICT literacy are also crucial skills. Blended Learning is applied in teaching and learning through media and technology in the form of online learning. Students can learn by themselves and gain knowledge from educational materials that teachers provided from numerous kinds of resources. In addition, Collaborative Learning is one of the most required skills in 21st century; it can assist students to learn through group process, teamwork, group activities, and exchanging knowledge with each other. Therefore, this research focused on blended learning and collaborative learning to develop English communication skills of the university students in English Teaching Program. The objective of this research was to determine the effectiveness of blended learning and collaborative learning upon English communication skills of English Teaching Program students. The sampling of this research was 23 English Teaching Program students in the Faculty of Education, Phranakhon Si Ayutthaya Rajabhat University. The research instruments were lesson plans, Pre-test and Post-test, and observation forms. The statistics employed in the research were Means, Standard Deviation (S.D.), and t-test. The results revealed that learning achievement of English communication skills after using the Blend Learning and collaborative learning was higher than before using the approach with statistically significant difference at .05 level. The levels of communication skills of English Teaching program students are in high levels ( X = 3.86). The results exposed positive results with outstanding effect. Consequently, the Blended Learning and the Collaborative Learning can be applied in English communication skill development. This research could be used as a guideline for English teachers to teach by using blended learning and support collaborative learning to develop students' English abilities. Five steps in blended learning with collaborative learning upon English communication skills are: 1) giving source of information 2) making group of students 3) task assignments 4) consulting teacher and 5) creating and publishing their works.

articleTitle: STEM Education Activities Development to Promote Computational Thinking’s Students
abstract: This research aims to develop STEM learning activities for promote student's computational thinking skills and the results of this learning activities toward computational thinking of senior school student in the computing classroom. The study groups were 30 secondary school students in Pranakorn Si Ayutthaya who were studying in Semester 1, Academic Year 2019. They were selected by purposive sampling method. The research instruments were; (1) STEM education lesson plans for computational thinking developments; (2) The student's journals; and (3) Computational thinking test. The research was divided into three phases. The first phase focused on design lesson plans and learning activities for developing student's computational thinking skills. The second phase is implement the lesson plans and learning activities with the study group. The third phase is evaluation of the effectiveness of learning activities on develop student's computational thinking skills. The results shown learning activities can develop student's computational thinking skills, because of these activities were challenged students with real everyday life problems that required to used their computational thinking to solve the problems by decompose problems, find pattern recognition, abstraction thinking and develop algorithm for computer programming. So, these STEM learning activities could be effectively used in Computing course.

articleTitle: Virtual Reality of Solar Farm for the Solar Energy System Training
abstract: This article presents the virtual reality solar farm model (VRSF) for using solar energy training to the trainees or any people who interest in the solar energy system. The trainees could learn as in real situations. It also decreases the cost and difficulty of training in real locations. VRSF has divided into 4 points which are solar farm, substation, control room, and battery charge chamber. In each point has an icon (i) to explain the information of the solar farm system in the format of the video, message, or picture. It also links to nearby placed locations upon the map defining and display via the website: www.vr-solarfarm.com. The result is found that VRFS for the solar energy training system is at a high-quality level, a mean value of 4.22 (S.D. value of 0.64). It was suitable and advantageous for solar energy training with satisfaction means the value at 4.26 (S.D. value of 0.58), at a high level. the learning achievement of the sample group found that the sample group was increased their knowledge after training up 80%. It is concluded that has good performance and suitable for use in training on the solar energy system. The education, which emphasizes science and technology or can (be) called STEM Education.

articleTitle: Student Development towards Innovation in The Information Engineering Curriculum of Faculty of Engineering, KMITL
abstract: This article presents the student development towards creative works of innovation in the Information Engineering curriculum of the Faculty of Engineering, King Mongkut's Institute of Technology Ladkrabang by using the theory of cognition in wisdom, skill range, and mental range. Enlighten students have knowledge and skills in creating innovative inventions. The satisfaction survey results in the integration of teaching and learning. The criteria were at a high level (4.03), which is 80.76 percent and the achievement of students' creative innovation works is at a high level (4.16), representing 83.31 percent.

articleTitle: The Effectiveness of the Quizizz Interactive Quiz Media as an Online Self-Assessment of Undergraduate Students to Improve Students’ Learning Outcomes
abstract: The purposes of the study were 1) to determine the effectiveness of an interactive quiz by using Quizizz feature, a web-based assessment tool, to improve students' learning outcomes and 2) to survey students' opinion toward online self-assessment by using Quizizz. The research used the quantitative and quality approach with experiment. The participant was 60, second year students who enrolled in English for communication course in the second semester of the 2020 academic year. The population comprised of 30 students in teaching English program, faculty of education, and in western music program, faculty of humanities and social sciences, Phranakhon Si Ayutthaya Rajabhat university, selected by using a purposive sampling technique. The research instruments were 1) the pretest and posttest to investigate on grammar, as much as 30 multiple choices questions which have been testing the validity of the expert validators, 2) the online questionnaire on opinions toward online self-assessment by using Quizizz, and 3) the interview to find out more in-depth data on students' self-assessment by using Quizizz. The experiment period was 4 weeks. The statistics method used to analyze data were mean, standard deviation, and Paired-sample T-test. The research findings were 1) the students' posttest score was higher than the pretest. The research was statistically significant difference at .05 level. The students were able to do self-assessment as a result of their learning outcomes by Quizizz: do the first quiz (pretest) - receive feedback - review - replay the quiz (posttest) - receive feedback - reflect, and 2) The students' opinions toward online self-assessment by using Quizizz were the high level. The total of result was (x̅ = 4.63, S.D = 0.49)., including with 1) the attitude (x̅ = 4.82, S.D = 0.54), 2) the convenience (x̅ = 4.74, S.D = 0.43), and 3) the content (x̅ = 4.67, S.D = 0.35) respectively. The participants had an overwhelmingly positive attitude towards online self-assessment by using Quizizz.

articleTitle: An Approach for Mental Preparation for First-Year College Students: A Case Study of Engineering Students
abstract: As first-year university students prepare to head to classes, many of them are worrying about how they will handle new responsibilities and workloads. Often, they fail to prioritize their learning needs due to anxiety. Hence, this paper presents a case study to illustrate a mindfulness meditative approach for helping electrical and computer engineering students to alleviate their anxiety during transition from high school to college. A sample of 44 first-year students at Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Thammasat University, voluntarily completed questionnaire after participating mindfulness training exercise. The survey results indicate their good satisfactions.

articleTitle: A Study of Learning Achievement using Social Media and Digital Video of Students in the Faculty of Education
abstract: Social media is one of the most popular technology used for many purposes. It is widely used so people tend to expert in using various tools available on social media. It could be used for communication, discussions, making recommendations on web boards or chat. Therefore, social media has been applied in teaching and learning process in the current epidemic situation. In addition, video is one of the most popular type of media. It is able to present useful information for teaching and learning including text, images and animation. Students could perceive some knowledge in many ways trough looking and hearing. Currently, the video has been developed in form of a digital system that is easy to produce. Teachers can use a video camera, camera or camera on their smartphones to shoot digital video. After that, the digital video has been edited with a computer program in order to make the complete video with full of content that would be suitable in teaching. The teachers could post their videos on social media and let students come to study at any time. This research focuses on the study of learning achievement using social media and digital video of students in the faculty of Education. The sampling of the study were the university students in the faculty of Education, Phranakhon Si Ayutthaya Rajabhat University. The research instruments were social media, digital videos, questionnaires and the tests. The statistics used in the research were the Means, Standard Deviation and T-Test. The results of the study have been showed that students in the faculty of Education had higher learning achievement significantly.

articleTitle: Management of Integrated Learning Approach for Electrical Installation Practice Skills
abstract: This paper concerns the management of integrated learning approach for electrical installation practice skills. The study aims to develop teaching and learning approach by focusing on learners in class and learners' involvement in the activities according o integrated instruction. The instrument used in this research includes a teacher handbook, teaching media such as demonstration and training packages, computer media, and an evaluation form. The trail of the developed teaching model is made for Electrical Technology course with samples of students of Faculty of Industrial Technology at Chitralada Technology Institute. It was found that the teaching and learning management model based on integrated instruction promotes den involvement on the design of teaching and learning activities, and their ability to select learning methods that are suitable for their existing knowledge and aptitude. In addition, the practice-based activities enhance students working skill, work experience, and teamwork. Moreover, students were satisfied with the teaching and learning activities which promote working skills to support technology education effectively and produce graduates with capabilities according to the real needs of industrial sector.

articleTitle: Teaching Requirement Engineering Using Industrial-Infused Project-Based Learning
abstract: This paper reports the result of an exploratory study conducted to assess (1) the achievement of learning outcomes (LOs) and (2) the perceived effectiveness of students' learning from Industrial-Infused Project-Based Learning (II-PrBL). The experiment and evaluation were made on the Software Engineering (SE) students in second year who enrolled in the 977-271 Requirement Engineering and System Modeling (RESM) course, semester 1/2019. The result shows that the students were able to think, analyse, integrate and apply the knowledge and skills achieved from the lecture to the real practice in problem-solving based on the industrial case study. They were able to achieve the necessary LOs for the RE course in both specific (hard) and generic (soft) skills. Furthermore, this II-PrBL resulted in the high perceived effectiveness of students' learning and the strong level of satisfactory teaching.

articleTitle: Effective Teaching Management through Cooperative Online Learning Activies for Engineering Education
abstract: The research purpose aims 1) to manage cooperative learning activities in training of engineering students, 2) to evaluate the efficiency of the teaching and learning process for electrical engineering course. The research tool consists of training plan, work sheets, electronic slides, instructional media and achievement test. Sample group was 18 trainees who were bachelor students or interesting peoples at Thepsatri Rajabhat University, Lopburi, Thailand. The research results shown that 1) the efficiency of the teaching and learning process through cooperative learning activities agreed to the standard criteria of Meguigan's efficiency formula and the comparison of learning achievement between the pretest and posttest found that is different of statistically significant at the .05 level, 2) the trainees' satisfaction with the developed learning and teaching process was at a high level (the average equaled to 4.40). It can be seen that the cooperative learning activities implemented in training course can encourage the learners to have the knowledge and skills in the 21st century and can be used appropriately in the teaching of engineering curriculum.

articleTitle: Experimental based Learning and Teaching Management for Localizer Transmitter of Aircraft Instrument Landing System
abstract: The purpose of this research was to manage an experimental based learning and teaching for localizer transmitter of aircraft instrument landing system. The research methodology is as follows: to study the learning and teaching problems on the navigation aid system course, to develop the MISDOP based student-centered learning process in practical teaching, to develop the localizer transmitter laboratory, and to evaluate the quality of the experimental based learning and teaching process. The results shown that the expert's opinions on the developed MISODOP based learning process were found reasonably at a high level. The developed localizer transmitter of aircraft instrument landing system can be used effectively in the teaching of the navigation aid system course and it can be applied to test localizer receiver on real aircraft while in a hangar.

articleTitle: Fire Alert System & Application Based on Internet of Things for STEM Education
abstract: In this paper, a methodology of fire alert system based on Internet of Things for STEM educational purposes is proposed to create awareness among users regarding fire emergencies in their threshold despite the user’s absence. It is deployed onto an IoT platform, where users could monitor their safety and receive images of fire emergency in their corresponding room via Line. This is integrated to reduce false alarms and activates actuators such as water-sprinkler and exhauster to extinguish class A and B fire types.

articleTitle: STEM Activity Through Design Based Learning in PM 2.5 Crisis for High school
abstract: STEM education is a way to promote design process implementation so that students can create solutions using science and mathematics knowledge and skills. This study examined students' STEM learning related to PM 2.5 pollution. In total, 75 grade 12 students from a large school in Bangkok, Thailand, participated in this study, which was collaboratively led by a science teacher, a science educator, a scientist, an engineer, and a mathematics educator. A qualitative methodology was used to analyze students' STEM understanding based on multiple data sources: a post-unit survey, a worksheet, reflective journal entries, and interviews. Seven categories of understanding emerged. Most students mentioned that design was a very important process and that they applied a design process when creating their PM 2.5 detector. Some students indicated the use of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics knowledge in their PM 2.5 detector design. However, most students indicated science and technology as core disciplines for their design; mathematics and engineering were less frequently mentioned among this group of students. More than 50% of the students referred to STEM-related skills, such as entrepreneurship, communication, problem solving, and collaboration, which they used to successfully develop their design. The design-based learning approach was useful in encouraging the students to apply the design process to solve real-world problems. They defined the problems in context or specific situation, collected data, generated alternative ideas, chose the best solution, created and tested a prototype, and evaluated and redesigned the prototype.

articleTitle: VHDL Implementation of ARM Cortex-M0 Laboratory for Graduate Engineering Students
abstract: Currently most of undergraduate and graduate level laboratory courses on microprocessor design belong to old curriculum and use extremely aged non-pipelined architectures which has no real connection to modern contemporary processors. Laboratory boards based on classic processors such as Intel 8051, 8085/86, Motorola 68000 are kept being used due to ease of teaching and simplicity of the architectures. In this paper a VHDL implementation of ARM Cortex-M0 which is a common pipelined processor used widely in modern embedded systems (such as STM32F microcontroller which uses ARM processor cores) is proposed. The implementation process divided into several steps which then can be used as a series of laboratory modules for teaching advanced microprocessor laboratory courses in universities. The core employs a 3-stage pipeline and implements all 16-bit Thumb and six 32-bit instructions all belonging to ARMv6-M architecture. Low cost FPGA development boards can be used to implement the design and conduct the proposed lab sessions.

articleTitle: Integrating MIAP Learning Activities Management and Cooperative Learning using Internet of Things Learning Package
abstract: The research aimed to develop a learning activities model using MIAP learning and cooperative learning. The five steps taken were 1)defining a sample group, 2)design of learning activities model, 3) development of research tools, 4)evaluation of research tools, and 5)implementing with a sample. The subjects in this study were composed of 38 in class 6/5 of Satrinonthaburi School. Research tools used in this study were 1)learning management plan, 2)Internet of Things experiment, 3)activity exercise, 4)learning achievement test, 5)learning behavior assessment questionnaire, and 6)questionnaire for the opinions of learners towards patterns of learning activities. Data were analyzed using statistics percentages, mean, standard deviation, and dependent t-test. The results of this research were as follows: 1)the result of learning efficiency was at 80/80. The result of the ability in the internet of things learning was 87.55 (E1), and the knowledge gained was 81.68 (E2). 2)The differences in students' learning outcomes of students' knowledge before and after being taught by this model were statistically significant at the.01 level. The students' learning outcomes after learning were higher than before the learning. 3)The students' opinions towards the learning activities model revealed that students agreed with all opinion statements at a high level.

articleTitle: AI-based Rock-Paper-Scissors plug and play system
abstract: In this paper, we present a plug and play Rock-Paper-Scissors game set that utilizes CNN-based static hand gesture recognition and a Markov chain-based bot. Each game round, the camera output is fed to the neural network and the hand gesture result is compared to the current Markov chain state. We utilize a CNN trained with a dataset containing rock-paperscissors hand gestures and unwanted inputs, and a multi-state Markov chain. Automated tests confirm the bot prediction capabilities and practical tests verify the precision of static hand gesture recognition. Tests against a verification dataset reveal a recognition accuracy of 97.4%.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit Encompassing Electrical and Mechanical Parts of Direct Current Motors
abstract: In this paper, a novel equivalent circuit of DC motors, which encompasses both electrical and mechanical parts, is presented. This equivalent circuit, which is more compact than the previously reported and requires only passive elements, allows for simulations of circuits containing DC motors to be carried out using SPICE program. Simulation and experimental results are shown to be in good agreement with theoretical calculation. The concept of this new equivalent circuit contributes to the understanding of DC motor operation using basic electrical circuit analysis.

articleTitle: The Development of Mastery Learning Self-Study Package for Air-Conditioning System Practice Skills
abstract: This paper aims to develop a mastery learning self-study package for air-conditioning system practice skills. The process started with the development of a mastery learning self-study package that contains five steps including 1) acquisition, 2) fluency, 3) maintenance, 4) application, and 5) adaptation. After that, a learning self-study package about air-conditioning system was developed containing a course syllabus, content sheet and assignment sheets, pre-test and post-test, worksheets, a test, a demonstration set, and a training set. Next, the package was evaluated by five experts in related field. The result revealed that the package is very suitable. The mastery learning self-study package was then tested applying purposive sampling to select a sample of 12 students enrolling in Air-Conditioning System course of Faculty of Industrial Technology, Chitralada Technology Institute. The results of the study indicated that: 1) the mastery learning self -study package is efficient at 83.37%, higher than the standard (75%); 2) the post-test scores are significantly higher than those of the pre-test at.05; and 3) students are very satisfied with the mastery learning self-study package.

articleTitle: Development of Simulation Based RISDA Learning Process for Electronic Technology Education
abstract: This research presents the development of the simulation based RISDA teaching and learning process for electronic technology education. The research methodology begins with a survey collected from stakeholders based on the requirements of graduate's users, then develops a simulation-based learning and teaching process called the RISDA learning model. The process comprises of 5 stages: R: Recall, I: Information, S: Simulation, D: Discussion, and A: Assessment. The research tools such as teacher manuals, activity plans, teaching materials and quizzes were designed. The results shown that the constructed research tools were suitable with the evaluated level of “very appropriate” (Mean equaled to 4.15) and the learners who completed the RISDA learning process were satisfied with the satisfactory level of “very satisfy” (Mean equal to 4.23). The learners had gained the expected learning outcomes that are aligned with the 21st Century learning skills and met the entrepreneurial needs.

articleTitle: A Study of Health Service Accessibility in Aging Society and Technological Development: A Case of the Urban Community Surround Sirinthorn Hospital, Bangkok
abstract: The situation of health in aging society and the issues on travelling in city communities in Bangkok have a relationship with its environment where is under an investigation of health activities and patterns of travelling among the elderly. This research aims to examine health activities, patterns of travelling and factors influencing health service assess in city communities among the elderly. Following the objectives of the present study, suggestions for further development are given to relevant departments.The major findings of the situation on travelling and problems on receiving health service of the elderly who have lived in city communities of Sirindhorn hospital, Bangkok leads to some recommendations for developing patterns of travelling for health service, designing activities for the elderly with different ages to have appropriate health service and promoting an engaging environment in the communities.

Author Keywords: city communities of Sirindhorn hospital Bangkok

articleTitle: Improving Graphic Design Skill Through G Suite for Education in Undergraduate Students
abstract: The purpose of this research was to answer how learning with G Suite for Education contribute toward improve graphic design skills and academic achievement of undergraduate students. The sample group used in this research was students in Bachelor of Education program that registered in Computer Graphic Design course at Phranakhon Si Ayutthaya Rajabhat University, Thailand. The evaluation of learning outcomes demonstrated the effectiveness of students' graphic design skills. Regarding G Suite, it was a tool that supports students in developing 21st-century specific skills, including self-learning skills, promoting collaborative learning anywhere, anytime, and all forms of technology, when connect their network to the Internet. Productivity tools for create, share and edit files in real-time in the cloud computing can also increase classroom management efficiency. In this research, students were tasked with practicing graphic design skills using a computer program in the process to help each other in the classroom, where the instructor was closely guided. Additionally, students practiced graphic design in class and homework, learn theories on their own from a G Suite environment, and practice graphic design in the classroom. Students were evaluated with actual conditions assessment by instructor using multiple scoring scales using a quality developed four-level rubric. The results indicated that G suite for Education enhanced students' creativity, design knowledge and Technology knowledge in term of graphic design skill and the student achievement was significantly higher at.05. Positively, students presented high satisfaction for experience in self-directed learning through the G Suite for Education environment.

articleTitle: Intelligent Fuzzy Logic for STEM-ED in Power Transformer Failure Investigation Based Power Utility Practice
abstract: The research in this article describes the development of a STEM based teaching tool for a computer programing in electrical engineering course. The research tool applies a Graphical User Interface simulation program for fault analysis by using Total Dissolved Combustible Gas and Key Gas method. The sampling group consisted of 21 students enrolling in the computer programing course. The quality evaluation of the tool from 5 experts indicates a satisfactory result in average of 4.07 out of 5 as a maximum point. The developed teaching set was effective at 1.06 in accordance with the standard criteria using Meguigans's theory. Learning achievement between pre-test and post-test was significantly different at the level of 0.05. This development of teaching and learning tool can be used effectively in teaching of electrical engineering education.

articleTitle: Case study: To identify the students that participating in the Cheer activity of the Faculty of Engineering, KMITL by using Near Field Wireless communication
abstract: This article presents wireless communication technology with NFC. In this case study, it is about using the NFC to identify the freshmen one by one that participating in the Cheer activity of the Faculty of Engineering, KMITL of the first-year students of 800 students, duration ten days. From the experiment results, when using the application, it can be used to check the names of students who have participated in the activity with 100 percent accuracy.

articleTitle: Air Turbulence Forecasting of Airbus type A320 in Southeast Asia using Deep Learning Method
abstract: This paper is present the Air Turbulence Forecasting of Airbus type A320 in Southeast Asia using the Deep Learning Method. It will collect flight data of aircraft in the region of Southeast Asia (Thailand and Vietnam). In which data was collected for 40 flights to forecast the occurrence of air turbulence in 3 status consist of non-turbulence, the rapid decrease and increase the altitude is out of pilot control. In this research using deep learning with supervise learning and create the mathematical model for air turbulence forecasting which could help to reduce the wastage that may affect to the passenger. The results, using 5 layers of deep learning (1 input layer, 3 hidden layers, and 1 output layer). The most suitable model consists of 9 features such as vertical speed, calibrated altitude, wind speed, wind direction (wind angle), temperature, latitude, longitude, true airspeed, and indicated airspeed. The output layer consists of 3 classes (class1=non-turbulence, class2=increase altitude, and class3=decrease altitude) and optimization the weight with gradient descent. The epoch number is 1500 and the learning rate is 0.1, which will get accuracy 88% for the train set and 86 % for the test set.

articleTitle: Assessment Design for Learning by Online Business Game
abstract: The purpose of this research is to present a methodology designed for assessing learning outcomes from online business games. In the qualitative part of the assessment, the instructions are written to test skills acquired after playing a game compared with the cognitive learning outcomes. This study use data collected from 66 third-year undergraduate university students in Thailand. The results show that game participants after playing the game can apply theoretical knowledge, break the game down to workable segments, use information to make decisions, act as leaders to make plans, take managerial roles and manage risk. A remarkable point is the ability for participants to identify conflicts in a team, and then use soft skills to manage conflicts and to solve problems by themselves.

articleTitle: Vertical Speed Prediction for the Efficient Landing of Aircraft Using GRU
abstract: Air traffic management is currently the process of managing air traffic demand. For support the capacity to handle the amount of air traffic. Whether it is in the airspace sector or the airport area. There are many factors such as the ability of the air traffic providers, physical characteristics of airspace and airport terrain. The main goal of air traffic management is to manage air traffic control. Streamlined and demand-capacity balancing are safe and effective. Whether it is air traffic service providers or passengers. In this research, the experiment was carried out on specific aircraft model A-320. Traveling from Bangkok Suvarnabhumi Airport to Phuket International Airport. In which the landing airport has island terrain. Therefore, requires high security due to physical characteristics in the airspace which has many factors such as wind and wind direction and to provide safety and effective landing. Therefore, take the factors affecting the landing to predict the vertical speed. The epoch =2000, learning rate =0.01, accuracy more than 90% for training set and 90% for test set.

articleTitle: Leadership in the Digital Era
abstract: Many corporations invest in building their digital capabilities, hoping to drive business competencies and become leaders amid the disruptive era. Digital capability shapes desired workforce skills and attitude; hence, the objective of this study is to identify factors involved in shaping both workforce attitudes and learning capabilities within today's fast-changing environment. The quantitative research surveyed all levels of employees from ground staff to top-level management, including entrepreneurs. The dataset consisted of samples from 41 nationalities based on the International Institute for Management Development (IMD), World digital ranking 2019. Research findings explain how having the right mindset contributes to educational successes and how knowledge sharing leads to collaborative workforce in the digital era. Business leaders can apply these findings in setting a strategic direction to education.

articleTitle: Study of Teacher’s Learning Management Behavior with Professional Learning Community through Active Learning in Mathematics Classroom
abstract: This research aimed to study teacher's learning management behavior with Professional Learning Community through Active Learning in Mathematics. The qualitative methods employed were intensive data collection, content analysis, in-depth interviews, The key informants were 1) 3 Experts in Professional Learning Community based on Lesson Study 2) Teachers who involved in Professional Learning Community based on Lesson Study. The data were analyzed by inductive method and verified by triangulation technique in order to find relevant data to Study of teacher's learning management behavior with Professional Learning Community through Active Learning in Mathematics. The results show that Study of teacher's learning management behavior with Professional Learning Community through Active Learning in Mathematics were In overall, the teachers had learning management behaviors that emphasized on the learners in the high level (= 2.71, SD = 0.13), with the highest learning management behaviors, namely the importation of lessons (= 3.00, SD = 0.00) in the use of media and learning resources (= 3.00, SD = 0.00) in the organization of learning activities (= 2.76, SD = 0.16) and in the evaluation (= 2.71, SD = 0.13) respectively.

articleTitle: Pre-service Teachers’ Perceptions on Active Learning in Basic Mathematics Measurement in School Course
abstract: This study aimed to explore pre-service teachers perceptions of the use of active learning in basic mathematics measurement in school course. The qualitative methods employed were data collection use observation in classroom reflection form and interview target group. The data were analyzed by content analysis from three parts of data about pre-service teachers perceptions of the use of active learning in basic mathematics measurement in school course. The results show that pre-service teachers perceptions about active learning are working group, learning by a hands-on activity, solving the problem by themselves, share ideas with friends, and playing games and competition.

articleTitle: A Comparison Study Between CATC Commercial Pilot-Airplane Course and the Course with EASA Standards
abstract: This paper studies the Civil Aviation Training Center (CATC) commercial pilot-airplane course and the course with the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) standards. The purposes of this paper are the comparison of the differences between the current CATC commercial pilot-airplane course and the course with EASA standards, and to be used as a guideline for the development of the CATC courses. This paper covers the course structure, the pattern for training examination and assessment, the organizational structure and staff, the instructional equipment and the facility requirements. Gap analysis methods and interviewing experts from CATC and from the Civil Aviation Authority of Thailand (CAAT) were used. As the results, the CATC course and the course with EASA standard are difference in 4 parts except the facility requirements. Overall, the guidelines described in this paper are for fulfilling the gap at the beginning.

Author Keywords: the Commercial Pilot License - Aeroplane Course

articleTitle: Students’ Perceptions of Makerspaces and Learning Environments in Thai Schools
abstract: Makerspaces were created more than five years ago in schools and many other places. However, many makerspaces have either closed down or are occupied by fewer users than expected, negatively affecting the number of new innovations being brought onto the market. The findings show interesting facts concerning the environment of makerspaces in Thai schools. It is now time for schools to redesign their makerspaces.

articleTitle: Study of Applied STEM Education with Turbine Engines Topic for the Commercial Pilot License – Aeroplane Course
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to apply STEM education through gas turbine topic that will be taught in the Commercial Pilot License - Aeroplane Course in the future. The initial study was made on STEM and gas turbines. Therefore, we integrated the knowledge from the digestion of gas turbines with the STEM education. The statistical results show that the analytical content of Engineering literacy in STEM method was the most remarkable percentage. Consequently, we should apply engineering knowledge to be a part of major content in gas turbine subject. The part of Engineering in STEM was also significance for improving to complex content in this subject to make it easier to learn.

Author Keywords: the Commercial Pilot License – Aeroplane Course (EASA)

articleTitle: Creation of Pinhole Camera for Solar Eclipse Using STEM Education
abstract: The STEM education was used in this study to develop the science skills of undergraduate students. They can generate the instrument for solar eclipse observation by themselves. It is corresponding to the evaluation which the overall is 4.75 that means the learning by doing process will help develop learners a lot. Furthermore, the overall satisfaction from the pinhole camera user is 4.84 that means the instrument was created from this process is easy for both usability and knowledge.

articleTitle: Development of Interdisciplinary Integrated Teaching Model on Sensor Technology and Applications for Industrial Education
abstract: The objective of this research is to develop and evaluate the efficiency of an interdisciplinary integrated teaching model on sensor technology and applications for industrial education. The research starts with the development of an interdisciplinary integrated teaching model based on STEAM education approach which consists of six steps including preparation, pre-learning, information, activity, discussion, and assessment. The developed instructional package for sensor technology and applications include a lesson plan, information sheets, worksheets, an achievement test, a simulation program, PowerPoint presentations, and an experimental set. The quality of teaching model was evaluated by five experts. The results revealed a high level of appropriateness. Then, the teaching model was applied to 21 bachelor students at the Faculty of Industrial Technology, Chitralada Technology Institute. The results illustrated that 1) The results show that the quality of the developed interdisciplinary integrated teaching model was more appropriate. 2) the developed instructional package was efficient with 78.33/79.76; 3) the score of the post-test was significantly higher than that of the pre-test when comparing the learning progress (.05); and 4) the students was highly satisfied.

articleTitle: Selection of Terminal Device for Virtual Simulation Experiment
abstract: With the development of virtual reality technology, different kinds of terminal device were employed in virtual simulation experiment teaching, and many new release forms of virtual experiment came out. The feature of human-computer interaction in different kinds of terminal device was analyzed in this paper, and the demands for human-computer interaction feature of different learning aims were specified. Combined the impact of different virtual experiment systems release forms on the virtual experimental environment, a suggested solution was proposed for virtual experiment designer choosing a proper releasing terminal device. At last, 527 virtual experiments were selected from candidates for national virtual simulation experiment teaching projects in 2019, and the suggested solution was employed to assess these experiments. As a result, 12% of experiments were released in improper terminal, this indicated that there are existing misunderstandings when the virtual experiment system designer choosing terminal device.
